method: book places from Goodreads publisher blurbs + LitRes opening-chapter previews; real layouts from Wikipedia articles (fetched via API)

sites.name: THE WHALEBONE SHORE
sites.shape: a dying arctic coast village that wants outsiders for an offering
sites.notes: Gravel streets on permafrost, every house up on pilings; the fight is a whiteout siege across open sea ice with the airstrip as the only extraction.

source.notes: book sends the crew from an arctic gateway onto frozen tundra where a dwindling coastal people hold a grim rite; the book names no town, this is our real arctic-coast pick

sites.name: THE LISTENING POST NINE
sites.shape: abandoned cold-war radar station on the tundra
sites.notes: A long linked module building, a radome and a gravel strip on the flat coast: a scavenger set piece between tundra villages.

source.notes: cold-war radar line ruins fit the book's arctic leg; our pick, the book does not name this station

sites.name: THE BOG-IRON HAMLET
sites.shape: rebel camp hidden in a coastal pine forest
sites.notes: Sandy forest roads, a cedar-water millpond and a 40-site iron village: guerrilla fight in the pines.

source.notes: book's rebels hide in the coastal pine forest of the old New Jersey shore; our pick of a real village inside it

sites.name: THE GREAT AIRSHIP SHED
sites.shape: giant airship hangar on a pine-barrens base
sites.notes: One enormous arched shed (real Hangar One once held a 'largest single room' record) scaled to a walkable cathedral; fights happen under the roof.

source.notes: same pine-forest leg of the book; a real base in that forest, our pick

sites.name: THE OLD BARNEY POINT
sites.shape: lighthouse on a barrier-island inlet
sites.notes: The 50 m (real 163 ft) red-and-white tower on the inlet jetty is a sniper perch and a landmark seen from the whole coast.

source.notes: book's leg on the forested eastern-seaboard coast near the pine barrens; our coastal pick

sites.name: THE SKY MESA
sites.shape: a small canyon-country pueblo that offers strangers to the spirits
sites.notes: A real 111 m (365 ft) mesa top reached by rock stairs; terraced stone roomblocks, kivas and rock cisterns; the climb is the fight.

source.notes: book's small pueblo in the old New Mexico canyons is an invented town; this real sky pueblo is our stand-in for its shape

sites.name: THE BUTTE WALL
sites.shape: old dam project on a desert river that hides a lab
sites.notes: A 92 m (301 ft) concrete gravity dam with spillway and powerhouse; the crest road is a gauntlet and the galleries are a dungeon.

source.notes: book 73's canyon dam project hides the makers of acid-spitting beasts; book 80's war is fought along the Rio Grande; this real Rio Grande dam is our pick

sites.name: THE LEVEE CAMP

real.place: Henderson and the Atchafalaya Basin levee

sites.shape: bayou town where a healer raises mindless followers
sites.notes: Levee road on one side, a 20 mile wide swamp on the other; camps on pilings linked by boardwalks; the fight moves by flatboat.

source.notes: book 74's road runs from the desert southwest into the Louisiana bayous; book 77 heads into Cajun country for a cure; this real levee town is our pick

sites.name: THE CRAWFISH BRIDGE
sites.shape: Cajun river town where a hidden queen holds a cure
sites.notes: A main street of brick storefronts runs to a drawbridge over Bayou Teche; the town grew from a 1799 footbridge.

source.notes: book's crew follows a trail into Cajun country seeking a cure for a sickness; our real Cajun town pick

sites.name: THE LAST ISLAND CAMPS
sites.shape: storm-wrecked swamp-coast barony with a besieged port
sites.notes: One road (LA 1) and one bridge onto a long strip of camps raised on pilings; a hurricane-lashed siege set piece.

source.notes: book's crew is stranded by storms and pirates at a swamp barony on the Louisiana Gulf; the barony is invented, this real barrier island is our pick

sites.name: THE RIG YARD
sites.shape: swamp-coast oil port held by pirates
sites.notes: Louisiana's southernmost port: boat slips, pipe yards and tanks at the end of a flood-prone highway outside the levees.

source.notes: book's swamp-coast port is invented; this real oil port is our stand-in for the pirate-held harbor

sites.name: THE THOUSAND WINGS
sites.shape: desert barony outside Tucson where an unseen player draws a battle line
sites.notes: Rows of parked planes on a 2,600 acre desert lot (nearly 4,000 aircraft): a maze of wings for a running gunfight.

source.notes: book 75's line in the dust is drawn outside Tucson; book 76 continues the hunt across the southwestern desert; our real Tucson pick

sites.name: THE SAHUARITA SILO
sites.shape: sealed cold-war missile silo in the desert
sites.notes: Flat gravel pad above; the real site has a three-level control centre and an eight-level silo joined by blast-locked cableways.

bunker.notes: real: 3-level launch control centre + 8-level silo, 2.4 m walls, 3-ton blast doors, cableway tunnels

source.notes: cold-war silo south of Tucson; our pick for the tech-laden southwestern leg of the two-book arc

sites.name: THE VALLEY RAILHEAD
sites.shape: high-desert valley town hunted by man-eaters
sites.notes: A rail town on the edge of a broad valley ringed by the Blue and Wallowa Mountains; the hunt starts here at night.

source.notes: book opens in the wide Grande Ronde valley of Oregon where flesh-eaters snatch children

sites.name: THE MORAINE LAKE
sites.shape: cave-riddled mountains where man-eaters hide
sites.notes: A ribbon lake behind high glacial moraines with a 35 ft concrete outlet dam and lodge village at the south end; cave raid in the basalt.

source.notes: book chases the man-eaters east into the forested, cave-riddled Wallowa Mountains

sites.name: THE SNAKE GORGE GATE
sites.shape: deepest-canyon hideaway with a buried bunker
sites.notes: A canyon a mile deep below the Oregon rim; the dam spans the Snake with a powerhouse at its toe; descend the switchbacks.

bunker.notes: game-side: the book's buried bunker; the real dam has only galleries and a powerhouse

source.notes: book places a hidden pre-war bunker in Hells Canyon about a hundred miles from the valley; the real dam marks the canyon floor

sites.name: THE RIVER TERRACE
sites.shape: river-crossing trade town raided from the air
sites.notes: A 133-block historic district on the Ohio River terrace below a bluff: open streets, rooftops and a bomber overhead.

source.notes: book's crossroads town sits on the sluggish Ohio River in a dried-out Indiana, bombed by a restored biplane; the town is invented, this real Indiana river town is our pick

sites.name: THE TWIN LOCKS

real.place: Cannelton Locks and Dam, Ohio River

sites.shape: river lock gates commanding the Ohio crossing
sites.notes: A tainter-gated dam with two parallel locks (main 1,200 ft) on the Indiana bank; a lock-wall fight above churning water.

source.notes: Ohio River crossing in the same book; our real river-control pick

sites.name: THE STEAM ROW
sites.shape: biggest vice-and-trade town on the wasteland roads
sites.notes: Eight bathhouses in a row facing the main avenue with a promenade on the hill above; a dense vice street for brawls.

source.notes: book's huge vice-and-trade town in the Arkansas dust is invented; this real spa row is our stand-in for its shape

sites.name: THE IGLOO FIELDS
sites.shape: chemical-weapons depot in the Arkansas lowlands
sites.notes: 13,493 acres, 665 buildings and 271 earth-covered igloos: a grid of sod humps for a stealth crawl.

bunker.notes: real: 271 earth-covered storage igloos (single level, sealed doors)

source.notes: book's quake strands the crew in Arkansas; our real Arkansas military pick

sites.name: THE PASS OF THE NORTH

real.place: El Paso / Ciudad Juarez on the Rio Grande

sites.shape: border-river city torn by a baron war
sites.notes: Twin cities on a concrete-lined Rio Grande: a 1859 downtown grid, bridges and a cathedral; the war line runs along the river.

source.notes: book's barons fight a bitter war around the Rio Grande while an old enemy holds nerve gas; this real border city is our pick

sites.name: THE ADOBE GARRISON
sites.shape: desert army post holding a hidden gas stockpile
sites.notes: The Army's second-largest post (~1,700 sq mi range); old adobe walls in the officers club, a parade ground and motor pools.

source.notes: same Rio Grande war; our pick for the army post the book's gas cache evokes

sites.name: THE WEST DESERT RANGE
sites.shape: desert test range where a returned cyborg builds an empire
sites.notes: 801,505 acres of the Great Salt Lake Desert ringed by mountains on three sides; lab blocks, igloos and an army airfield.

bunker.notes: real: earth-covered test igloos and lab blocks; no confirmed deep bunker

source.notes: book's crew finds signs in Utah that a cyborg enemy has returned; our real Utah test-range pick

sites.name: THE BOMBER FLATS
sites.shape: salt-desert airfield on the slave-trail road
sites.notes: WWII base with three 8,100 ft runways and seven hangars at the Utah-Nevada line; slaver camp in the hangars.

source.notes: book 98's crew is drugged, robbed and sold on the Great Salt Lake Desert; our real desert-edge airfield pick (also fits book 81's Utah)

sites.name: THE WHITE MILE
sites.shape: searing salt pan crossing hunted by slavers and man-eaters
sites.notes: A perfectly flat white salt pan: the vehicle chase and horse-flight set piece; no cover for miles.

source.notes: book's horses gallop across the blazing salt desert of Utah toward a springs town forty miles off; the town is invented

sites.name: THE ROCK HARBOR
sites.shape: southernmost surviving Pacific port, a scavenged harbor town
sites.notes: A 177 m (581 ft) volcanic plug guards the bay mouth, a 4 mile bay runs south behind a sand spit, and three power-plant stacks rise behind the Embarcadero.

source.notes: book's crew lines up on the battered pier of Morro Bay, the last port on the Pacific coast

sites.name: THE CASINO COVE
sites.shape: island harbor town in the new Pacific isles
sites.biome_note: semi-arid channel island; nearest coastal biome
sites.notes: A crescent harbor of 2-3 storey buildings on a valley floor below hills, capped by a 12-storey-tall round casino on the point.

source.notes: book's villain rules the savage Pacific isles above a sunken southern California; our real channel-island town pick

sites.name: THE PRISONERS HARBOR RANCH
sites.shape: wild ranch island in the new Pacific isles
sites.notes: California's largest island (22 mi long): a cove wharf, an old ranch complex and sea caves for smuggling.

source.notes: same isles leg; our real channel-island pick

sites.name: THE RIM LODGES
sites.shape: canyon-rim refuge on the road to a bunker
sites.notes: A 1924 park plan: a village square at the rail terminus below the rim hotel, lodges strung along the canyon edge.

source.notes: the crew heads toward the Grand Canyon for the nearest bunker after fleeing a town

sites.name: THE LAST HIGHWAY TOWN
sites.shape: highway town terrorized by a costumed vigilante
sites.notes: Six-block historic downtown on the old highway and the rail terminus to the canyon; a bombed main street.

source.notes: book's ravaged town hires the crew against a napalm-throwing vigilante; the town is unnamed, our road-town pick near the canyon

sites.name: THE CONTAINER SHOAL
sites.shape: storm-cut barrier island where scavengers live by a grounded cargo ship
sites.notes: The world's longest barrier island (113 mi) broken into islets; a rusting cargo ship on the shoal is the village.

source.notes: book 84 has a cargo ship driven onto the shoal of Padre Island opposite the Corpus Christi Bay entrance, the causeway gone; book 85 sails from there

sites.name: THE DROWNED BAYFRONT
sites.shape: drowned port city at the mouth of a sulfur sea
sites.notes: A stepped seawall bayfront, half-drowned towers, the harbor bridge and the WWII carrier museum ship moored at North Beach.

source.notes: same book: the bay has swollen to drown the low-lying port city; our real view of that bayfront

sites.name: THE FLIGHT SCHOOL POINT
sites.shape: drowned naval air station on the gulf
sites.notes: A 20,000 acre WWII station (997 hangars, shops, barracks) on a point between Corpus Christi Bay and the Laguna Madre.

source.notes: same gulf leg; our real military pick on that bay

sites.name: THE HARBOR CASTLE

real.place: Fort San Juan de Ulua, Veracruz

sites.shape: island fortress of a blood-cult port empire
sites.notes: A colonial complex of fortresses, prisons and a palace on an island facing the port, begun 1535; vaults and bastions for a prison break.

source.notes: book's captured crew sails into Veracruz where electric lights blaze and a cult marks them for slaughter

sites.name: THE LIT PORT
sites.shape: lit, intact port city ruled by a sacrificial cult
sites.notes: A walled 18th-century port (1790 wall, Santiago bastion) around the Zocalo with the 1731 cathedral and city hall; the sacrifice plaza fight.

source.notes: same book: the lit city where the crew is marked for death

sites.name: THE MOUNTAIN SPA VAULT

real.place: The Greenbrier and its congressional bunker

sites.shape: rumoured untouched pre-war town in the West Virginia mountains
sites.notes: A white six-storey grand hotel on a mountain lawn; beneath its 1959-62 West Virginia Wing lies a cut-and-cover bunker built for Congress.

bunker.notes: real: cut-and-cover bunker under the West Virginia Wing, blast doors, dormitories, power plant; decommissioned 1992

source.notes: book's traders converge on a rumoured untouched pre-war town in the West Virginia mountains; the town is invented, this real resort-over-bunker is our stand-in

sites.name: THE RIVER BEND CAPITOL
sites.shape: peaceful river town where the crew trades for a cart
sites.notes: The Kentucky River makes a turn through town with Downtown and South Frankfort on opposite banks joined by five bridges; the capitol on the far bank.

source.notes: book's crew trades brass for a horse and cart at a peaceful town on the Kentucky River before a salt storm

sites.name: THE WALL GAP
sites.shape: dust-bowl badlands crossing for a trading convoy
sites.notes: A 1907 railroad town at the foot of the eroded Badlands Wall: pinnacles and gulches make the convoy ambush ground.

source.notes: book's trading convoy crosses the dust bowl of the Badlands; our real badlands-gap pick

sites.name: THE DRUGSTORE STOP
sites.shape: roadside convoy stop above the badlands
sites.notes: A 1907 rail-platted town strung along the old highway at the Badlands rim: a long store block and a sea of billboards.

source.notes: same convoy leg; our real roadside-stop pick

sites.name: THE BURIED CAPSULE
sites.shape: missile launch capsule under the plains
sites.notes: Topside a small fenced support building; below, a hardened launch control capsule. The field once held 150 missiles over 13,500 sq mi.

bunker.notes: real: one hardened launch control capsule reached by elevator; silo D-09 nearby

source.notes: cold-war silo field in the same badlands; our pick

sites.name: THE MISSOURI RAILHEAD

real.place: Mandan rail yards on the Missouri

sites.shape: refurbished rail line across the Dakota plains
sites.notes: An 1879 rail town on the west bank of the Missouri: depot, roundhouse, boxcar lines and elevators; the train-top fight.

source.notes: book's iron horse runs refurbished track across the flat Dakota plains; our real Dakota rail-town pick

sites.name: THE NORTH WING

real.place: Minot Air Force Base and missile field

sites.shape: plains base where the train's mind-control lab could hide
sites.notes: A SAC base 40 mi from Canada with bombers and a Minuteman field; its windowless blast-resistant data centre housed two 275-ton computers.

bunker.notes: real: blast-resistant data centre and field launch capsules

source.notes: our pick for the mind-reading ruler's hidden lab on the Dakota line; the book does not name the base

sites.name: THE WOLF ISLAND HARBOR
sites.shape: Lake Superior island where two rival lords fight over metal and salt
sites.notes: A 45 mi island of rock ridges and narrow harbors; Rock Harbor's lodge, cabins and marina face a 50 ft leaning 1855 lighthouse.

source.notes: book's crew emerges onto Lake Superior's big island where metal and salt are worth killing for

sites.name: THE COPPER HARBOR STOCKADE
sites.shape: mainland stockade port facing the island lords
sites.notes: A restored 1844 army post: whitewashed log buildings around a parade ground behind a stockade on the Keweenaw tip.

source.notes: our pick for a real mainland harbor facing the book's Lake Superior island

sites.name: THE STRATEGIC HOLE
sites.shape: hidden pre-war science sanctuary under the plains
sites.notes: 1890 Fort Crook brick quarters on a parade ground, the WWII bomber plant, and the 1957 strategic command HQ building over its underground command post.

bunker.notes: real: underground command post beneath the 1957 HQ building; depth/levels not verified here

source.notes: book's great plains between northern Kansas, Iowa and Nebraska hid a secret pre-war science sanctuary; our real plains command pick

sites.name: THE STEAMBOAT BLUFF
sites.shape: peaceful river-bluff community on the tri-state plains
sites.notes: Nebraska Territory's largest town in 1880, now a museum village on a bluff over the Missouri with a 1939 truss bridge.

source.notes: the book's peaceful Native plains communities have no named town; our real river-bluff pick near the Kansas-Iowa-Nebraska corner

sites.name: THE BLUFF CASTLE RUIN

real.place: Ha Ha Tonka castle ruins, Lake of the Ozarks

sites.shape: a brilliant ruler's town with laboratories in a maze below
sites.notes: A burned early-1900s stone mansion and water tower on a bluff over the Lake of the Ozarks; caves, sinkholes and a natural bridge below.

source.notes: book's ruler-scientist lives in old Missouri forest country with a maze of labs beneath his town; the town is invented, this real bluff ruin and its caves are our stand-in

sites.name: THE ENGINEER POST
sites.shape: Ozark army post that could seed a new civilization
sites.notes: A 1940 Ozark training post (engineer, MP and chemical schools); WWII wooden barracks and a POW cemetery.

source.notes: our pick for a real Missouri post in the book's forested region

sites.name: THE HEALING WATERS
sites.shape: convoy destination that sells waters of youth
sites.notes: A mineral springs resort in a creek valley: two-storey hotels with long verandas, a dozen boarding houses, spring pumps and bathhouses.

source.notes: book's convoy heads to a town in Tennessee said to hold waters of rejuvenation; the town is invented, this real springs resort is our stand-in

sites.name: THE SECRET CITY

real.place: Oak Ridge and the Y-12 complex

sites.shape: secret atomic city where a bunker's order forms point
sites.notes: A 1942 fenced government town in a 17 mi valley: prefab cemesto houses up the ridge, the uranium plant down the valley.

source.notes: the book's crew lands in a Tennessee bunker; our real Tennessee secret-site pick

sites.name: THE NAVY ROCK
sites.shape: abandoned naval station on an island fought over by a sea lord
sites.notes: The southernmost Channel Island, 21 mi long, owned by the Navy since 1934 and its last ship-to-shore live-fire range: shelling and beach landings.

source.notes: book's sea baron and his fleet hold the island and its abandoned naval station against a rising from the land

sites.name: THE SPARTA TRACT
sites.shape: army post with a bunker beneath and a flooded tunnel
sites.notes: 60,000 acres between Sparta and Tomah with one of the largest sets of WWII wooden barracks still standing; the 1911 magazine is the oldest building.

bunker.notes: game-side: the book's buried complex; the real post has no known deep bunker

source.notes: book's crew comes up under Fort McCoy through a wrecked underground complex

sites.name: THE WAREHOUSE WARD
sites.shape: lake city besieged by mutant interlopers
sites.notes: Masonry warehouses and factories between the Milwaukee River and Lake Michigan: a dense 4-6 storey grid for street defence.

source.notes: book's crew fights to save Milwaukee from mutant interlopers

sites.name: THE PIERHEAD
sites.shape: battered Lake Michigan shoreline at the city's mouth
sites.notes: The river mouth guarded by an 1872-established steel pierhead light at the end of a short pier, a breakwater beyond.

source.notes: book's battle is fought against the battered Lake Michigan shoreline

sites.name: THE GATEWAY RUIN

real.place: Gateway Arch grounds, Old Courthouse and Eads Bridge

sites.shape: concrete jungle on the great river held by a sick lord and a holy man
sites.notes: A 192 m (630 ft) steel arch on the levee, the domed 1839 courthouse at the head of the mall, the 1874 Eads Bridge to the north.

source.notes: book's crew is held in St. Louis by a river barony while hunting a runaway girl

sites.name: THE TERRA COTTA BLOCKS
sites.shape: rubble downtown north of the riverfront where big buildings still lean
sites.notes: Laveille's numbered/tree-named street grid; the 10-storey 1891 Wainwright terra-cotta tower among rubble; a pyramid-roofed courts tower.

source.notes: same book: the crew walks south through fields of rubble away from where the tall buildings stood

sites.name: THE MILE-HIGH STATION
sites.shape: mile-high city split by a civil war between two would-be rulers
sites.notes: Denver's 1858 original square mile: red-brick warehouses around the 1881/1914 Union Station at 17th and Wynkoop; the civil-war front line.

source.notes: book's crew comes out near the ruins of Denver, a city caught in a civil war

sites.name: THE NORTH POWERHOUSE
sites.shape: the power plant that gives the city its hope
sites.notes: A large power station 5 mi north of downtown Denver with stacks, cooling towers and a switchyard: the prize both armies want.

source.notes: book's Denver has a working power plant; our pick of the real plant north of downtown

sites.name: THE ARSENAL PRAIRIE
sites.shape: secret scientist enclave outside the mile-high city
sites.notes: A 1942 chemical weapons plant later leased to a pesticide maker, 8 mi NE of downtown: plant halls, tank farms, igloos and waste basins on open prairie.

source.notes: book's third player is a hidden enclave of scientists; our pick of the real chemical arsenal beside Denver

sites.name: THE CARP SHELTER
sites.shape: cold-war government shelter filled with weapons, vehicles and food
sites.notes: A four-storey underground reinforced concrete bunker (100,000 sq ft) under a grass mound 30 km west of Ottawa, entered by a long blast tunnel.

bunker.notes: real: 4-storey underground, 9,300 m2, blast doors, rated for 5 Mt at 1.8 km, filtered air

source.notes: book's convoy hunts the cold-war government shelters of Canada for stockpiles and four portable reactors

sites.name: THE LAKEHEAD ELEVATORS

real.place: Thunder Bay grain harbor on the Trans-Canada

sites.shape: lake port waypoint on the old Trans-Canada road west
sites.notes: Two merged lake cities (Fort William and Port Arthur) with grain elevators along Lake Superior; the main stop on the road west.

source.notes: book's convoy rides west on the old Trans-Canada Highway from north of Toronto; this real highway port is our waypoint pick

sites.name: THE PALACE OF LIGHT ALCOVE
sites.shape: a city carved in stone where mind-game masters hide missing children
sites.notes: North America's largest cliff dwelling: sandstone roomblocks, towers and kivas packed under an alcove above a canyon; ladders are the only way.

source.notes: book's crew tracks missing children into the canyons of Mesa Verde, Colorado, to a city carved in stone

sites.name: THE MESA-TOP HEADQUARTERS
sites.shape: mesa-top approach above the stone city
sites.notes: One of six buff-sandstone park buildings with projecting vigas on the mesa top; the trail drops into the canyon to the alcove villages.

source.notes: same book's canyon country; the real mesa-top approach

sites.name: THE REPUBLICAN RIVER SQUARE
sites.shape: civil-war-torn junction town under siege by flesh-eating sick
sites.notes: A planned Smoky Hills county seat on the Republican River, the 1907 Brown Grand opera house, and a 304-building WWII POW camp at a three-railroad junction.

source.notes: book's junction town in northern Kansas is invented; this real north-Kansas county seat and its railroad-junction camp are our stand-in

sites.name: THE LIMESTONE POST
sites.shape: cavalry post where a predark bioweapon could have escaped
sites.notes: A 1853 frontier post at the Republican-Smoky Hill junction built of native limestone around a parade ground over the Kansas River valley.

source.notes: our pick for the real north-Kansas military post near the book's outbreak country
